subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Collaborative Robots: Working Alongside Humans
description: A short lesson to help you apply Collaborative Robots: Working Alongside Humans.

hook.text: Traditional robots are caged behind fences. Cobots work right next to people, safely sharing the workspace.

buildup.text: Cobots use force-limiting joints. If they bump a person, they stop instantly before causing harm.

discovery.text: You can teach a cobot by physically guiding its arm through the motion. No programming language needed.

twist.text: Cobots are slower and weaker than industrial robots. Safety comes at the cost of speed and payload capacity.

climax.text: Small manufacturers adopt cobots because they're affordable, flexible, and don't need safety cages or expert programmers.

punchline.text: Strong enough to help. Gentle enough to trust. The robot you can stand next to.

quiz.question: What key safety feature allows cobots to work near humans without cages?
options: They operate in a separate area and never physically overlap with workers
Force-limiting joints stop the robot instantly upon contact with a person
They move so slowly that any collision would be harmless
